newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air mail at Frankfurt down 2.9pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Air mail at Frankfurt down 2.9pct in 1996.

text.p: Air mail volumes should improve at Frankfurt Airport in 1997 after a 2.9 percent decline in 1996, airport authority Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) forecast.
Flown air mail fell to 161,543 tonnes last year after Deutsche Post AG switched some overnight post distribution to road transport, an FAG report said.
Overnight post, which makes up 60 percent of air mail volumes, declined seven percent in 1996 with a 17 percent slump in the second half of the year, the FAG market research department report said.
The average nightly post volume at Frankfurt Airport fell to 370 tonnes in 1996 from 400 tonnes in 1995.
The decline was prompted by a new Deutsche Post network of Germany distribution centres and accompanying use of large containers for which insufficient air capacity was available, FAG noted.
"After completion of the new Deutsche Post transport logistics concept an increase in air mail volumes at Frankfurt can be expected for 1997," the report forecast.
International post, which accounts for 35 percent of Frankfurt air mail, rose 5.6 percent in 1996.

Top growth markets were North America, tourist destinations in southern Europe and refugee post to former Yugoslavia, the FAG report said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
